title.narrative: Resource Matters - transparency in the cobalt value chain
Resource Matters - transparens i värdekedjan kobolt

description.narrative:
Resource Matters is an international NGO, based in Brussels, Belgium, with a predominant focus on improved governance of natural resources. In the DRC context, this has led to a focus on the transparency of the extractive industry, as well as its links to the energy domain. It has a high credibility with an extensive network in the DRC. Since its founding 2017, it has a stellar reputation in the Congolese context. It works in close collaboration with local civil society groups, encouraging them to network and join forces for increased impact.
Resource Matters will receive support to build on its cobalt supply chain pilot map to offer a comprehensive overview of all actors along the chain to a wide variety of stakeholders involved in making the energy transition a reality. The present proposal lists technical improvements and a series of activities to ensure that the tool will effectively reach and be used by stakeholders. The new extended verison will not only include the source of the cobolt but also be connect to other platforms that report about violations of human rights and the environment. The contribution will also include capacity development for Resource Matters.

Resource Matters är en internationell icke-statlig organisation med säte i Bryssel, Belgien, som främst fokuserar på förbättrad förvaltning av naturresurser. I Demokratiska Republiken Kongo har detta lett till en fokusering på transparens inom utvinningsindustrin och dess kopplingar till energiområdet. Organisationen har hög trovärdighet och ett omfattande nätverk i Demokratiska Republiken Kongo. Sedan grundandet 2017 har den ett utmärkt rykte i den kongolesiska kontexten. Den arbetar i nära samarbete med lokala grupper i det civila samhället och uppmuntrar dem att skapa nätverk och slå sig samman för att få större genomslagskraft.
Resource Matters kommer att få stöd för att bygga vidare på sin plattform för värdekedjan för kobolt för att kunna erbjuda en omfattande översikt över alla aktörer längs kedjan till en mängd olika intressenter som är involverade i att göra energiomställningen till verklighet. I detta förslag anges tekniska förbättringar och en rad aktiviteter för att se till att verktyget effektivt når ut till och används av intressenterna. Den nya utökade versionen kommer inte bara att innehålla koboltets väg utan även kopplas till andra plattformar som rapporterar om kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter och miljö. Bidraget kommer också att omfatta kapacitetsutveckling för Resource Matters.

Resource matters(RM) has delivered on all objectives. The 4 main objectives as described in the annual report are: developing an online cobolt supply chain mapping tool, assist DRC in developing a national mineral strategy, strengthen the voice of civil society and improve their own organisational capacity.
The main results are:
1 Their cobolt chain mapping tool following the cobolt from the mine in DRC to end products has been improved and is probably the most detailed individual supply chain ever publicly documented
-It now includes both industrial and artisanal mine sites.
-It includes 347 companies, 240% more since its launch in 2022.
-It connects to the Business and Human Rights Resource Center so users can see potential social and environmental issues connected to different parts of the value chain.
-RM has succeeded with making the platform known and used through e.g. contact with companies in the value chain, radio and participating in different conferences/fora such as at the OECD forum on minerals, the EU Raw Materials week and Responsible Minerals Initiative. It has been used by companies, civil society, academia, media and international organisations such as IEA and OECD. Most users are from the western world and DRC but it has ad a global outreach. They have been asked to expand also to other minerals such a lithium and coltan. The amount of users per month of the platform increased with 148% the second year of the project.
-RM has shown that it is possible to track minerals
2 The DRC is now developing a national minerals strategy
-2 multistakeholder fora has been successfully organised moving the process forward, one in Kolwezi and one in Kinshasa
-A white paper used as a draft for the detailed discussions of the strategy has been written.
-Discussions from these forms has directly impacted policy as the government implemented a cobolt export ban in february 2025 inspired by discussions held at the forum in december 2024. Even though RM did not recommend a complete ban the governmentet wanted time to reflect on how to act and has later been in touch with RM to get more input.
3 Strengthened voice of civil society
-Coordinated the creation of a civil society strategic roadmap for the minerals sector
-Support to local civil society consortia within environment and social impacts has created direct dialogue with main company actors such as Umicore.
4 RM has improved as an organisation
-Improved strategic planning and strategic learning
-Improved financial management through implementation of a new financial managment system and transitioning to double entry accounting
-Implemented a new risk management system inlcuding staff safety and reducing risks of aggressive lawsuits
-Updated their code of conduct and HR manual resulting in for example change of 2 contracts and avoiding gender disparities in salary
The general opinion is that Resource Matters has delivered beyond the expectations. They have delivered on the activities planned and after seeing them in action on several international and national conferences and fora it is clear that they are very well respected and listen to of all actors in the sector. They have managed to find an approach where they can both very harshly criticize but at the same time have a very constructive dialogue with private sector, governments and civil society. They have proven to be a very skillful moderator. Technically they are very skilled. They have also during the entire project had a very open and direct dialogue with the embassy which has made it easy to follow their work and see both strengths and things to improve. They have really engaged to improve. For the embassy they have been a strong partner in dialogue but also a source of knowledge to better understand the mining sector. They have always been positive to contribute at events organised by the embassy. It is encouraging and impressing to see a small organisation that despite challenges such as political instability, personal safety, private crisis and aggressive lawsuits against them(to mention some) still continous to work hard and create results. They are one of few anti-corruption actors in the DRC and hence have an important role to play. Resource Matters needs to continue to improve their financial management skills and continue to work on their diversification of income but as a whole the embassy is very satisfied with the collaboration.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
